# clavis import

<p class="cli-lead">Import secrets from files or external providers</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis import [FILE] [flags]
```

</div>

Import `.env`, JSON or YAML files, or pull everything from another secret
manager. A folder is walked recursively and each file's directory becomes
the secret folder. Try `--dry-run` first: it shows what would be new,
changed or unchanged, never values.

## Examples

<p class="cli-example-title">A .env file</p>

```sh
clavis import .env
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Preview a folder</p>

```sh
clavis import ./config/ --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Rename keys while importing</p>

```sh
clavis import .env --map import-map.yaml
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Infisical</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider infisical \
  --remote-project "$INFISICAL_PROJECT" --remote-env dev \
  --token "$INFISICAL_TOKEN" --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Doppler</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider doppler \
  --remote-project my-project --remote-env dev \
  --token "$DOPPLER_TOKEN" --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao (KV v1 or v2)</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider vault \
  --base-url "$VAULT_ADDR" --vault-mount secret --vault-version 2 \
  --remote-path apps/web --token "$VAULT_TOKEN" --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">1Password Connect</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider onepassword \
  --base-url "$OP_CONNECT_HOST" --op-vault "$OP_VAULT" \
  --token "$OP_CONNECT_TOKEN" --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">AWS Secrets Manager</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider aws --aws-region eu-central-1 \
  --aws-access-key "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" --aws-secret-key "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" \
  --aws-prefix app/ --dry-run
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Google Secret Manager</p>

```sh
clavis import --provider gcp --gcp-project my-project \
  --gcp-service-account service-account.json --gcp-prefix APP_ --dry-run
```

## Details

A map file renames keys and folders; an empty target drops the key:

```yaml
keys:
  OLD_DATABASE_URL: DATABASE_URL
  DROP_ME: ""
folders:
  "": /imported
  legacy: /legacy
```

Provider credentials can also come from their usual environment
variables: `INFISICAL_TOKEN`, `DOPPLER_TOKEN`, `VAULT_ADDR`,
`VAULT_TOKEN`, `OPENBAO_ADDR`, `OPENBAO_TOKEN`, `OP_CONNECT_HOST`,
`OP_CONNECT_TOKEN`, `OP_VAULT`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`, `GCP_PROJECT` and
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`.

The web app's **Import** dialog accepts `.env` or JSON with the same
dry-run preview.
